definitions.explanation: A Japanese Buddhist festival to honor the spirits of ancestors, typically held in mid-August.

examples.japanese: お{盆|ぼん}に{故郷|ふるさと}に{帰|かえ}る。
examples.english: I return to my hometown during Obon.

examples.japanese: お{盆|ぼん}{休|やす}みに{旅行|りょこう}する。
examples.english: I travel during the Obon holiday.

examples.japanese: お{盆|ぼん}は{先祖|せんぞ}の{霊|れい}を{迎|むか}える{行事|ぎょうじ}だ。
examples.english: Obon is an event to welcome the spirits of ancestors.

notes:
お{盆|ぼん} (Obon) is one of Japan's three major holiday periods, along with {正月|しょうがつ} (New Year) and ゴールデンウィーク (Golden Week). It is a Buddhist festival honoring ancestral spirits.

TIMING:
Most of Japan observes Obon from August 13-16. Some regions (notably Tokyo) observe it in mid-July. Many companies give employees {盆|ぼん}{休|やす}み (Obon vacation).

CULTURAL TRADITIONS:
- {迎|むか}え{火|び}: welcoming fire (to guide spirits home)
- {送|おく}り{火|び}: sending fire (to see spirits off)
- {墓参|はかまい}り: visiting family graves
- {盆踊|ぼんおど}り: Bon dance (community festival dance)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- お{盆|ぼん}{休|やす}み: Obon holiday/vacation
- お{盆|ぼん}に{帰省|きせい}する: to return to one's hometown for Obon
